summary: Map thread coordinates to logical tensors and physical addresses without silently losing boundary elements.
outcomes: Derive flat and multidimensional indices for a given layout.
Handle tails, strides and index overflow explicitly.
sequence: Label each cell of a small rectangular array.
Connect block/thread coordinates to global indices.
Separate logical shape from stride and allocation size.
Add masks and grid-stride loops for irregular sizes.
Test transposed views, empty inputs and large index arithmetic.

visual.question: Which thread owns this output and which addresses does it read?
visual.interaction: Select a thread or output; highlight matching coordinates and masked lanes.

practice.task: Write a strided elementwise kernel supporting non-multiple sizes.
practice.success: Every valid output is written exactly once, boundaries remain intact and reference comparisons pass.
